title: What if you scooped ice cream on Mercury?
caption:
On Mercury's night side, ice cream would crack like glass. 🍨🪐

Mercury's night side drops to about −180 °C (NASA). Your freezer sits at −18 °C (FDA).

Ice cream is ice crystals held in a sugary syrup. Below roughly −28 to −32 °C that syrup turns into a brittle glass, so a spoon chips it instead of scooping.

The twist: a Mercury night lasts about 88 Earth days. When the Sun comes up, the ground reaches about 430 °C.

Send this to the friend who microwaves the ice cream tub to soften it.

Tomorrow: what if Earth stopped spinning?

⚠️ Don't try this. Ultra-cold food (dry ice, liquid-nitrogen desserts) can burn your mouth and skin.
